before: On the disco floor, the positions stayed fixed while the pattern changed. Here, different choices stand beside one another. You can go back to the first column.
after: On the disco floor, you held an arrangement before advancing to the next. Here, the choices stand beside one another. One column can remain in view while you look at its neighbour.

before: The geometry has stayed still. Follow the red past the blue sphere to the next block. The parts touch in one order; colour lets you gather them in another.
after: Follow the red past the blue sphere to the next block. The sphere keeps those two red parts apart, yet your eye can bring them together. The parts touch in one order; colour lets you gather them in another.

before: The third column assigns colour by height. Two blocks can now disagree. In the fourth, each colour is calculated from the one below: the hue moves halfway around the hue circle, then halfway again. Two colours alternate up the stack. A neighbour has become an input.
after: The third column assigns colour by height. A block near the floor and a block near the top receive different colours. Sharing a shape no longer gives them the same colour. In the fourth, each colour is calculated from the one below: the hue moves halfway around the hue circle, then halfway again. Ochre, blue, ochre again. The alternation is held in the column, for your eye to climb. A neighbour has become an input.
